topics.assessment: Fixed total mass of one pure substance; saturated-liquid endpoints and critical endpoint; source CK/liquid-region vocabulary preserved with fluid-only scope; P,V,T constrained rather than independent.
Saturated-vapor endpoints; AK/BK coexistence region, vanishing-phase boundaries and critical merging; total mass distinguished from changing phase masses and phase volumes.

Subcritical unsaturated vapor can condense by equilibrium isothermal compression; supercritical isothermal compression has no separated liquid-vapor transition in the stated fluid scope; ideal-gas behavior additionally requires low density.

native_contract.boundary_assessment: Liquid endpoints -> two-phase region -> unsaturated/supercritical states: all adjacent native anchors exact and concept transitions sensible.

topics.assessment: Temperature determines saturation pressure for a specified pure substance with both phases at equilibrium; not universal across substances or single-phase states.
Experimental p(T), critical pressure as coexistence-curve endpoint rather than absolute maximum pressure; faster pressure rise qualified by common initial state and dilute-vapor comparison.
Ideal-vapor approximation requires dilute gas, excludes unqualified near-critical use; original equation2-19 reference retained.
pV=(m/mu)RT retained exactly; mass belongs to vapor, mu is molar mass, T is Kelvin, SI units compatible.
V is vapor-occupied volume, not whole vessel including liquid.

Equilibrium isothermal compression/expansion exchanges phase mass while total mass stays fixed; both phases must remain. rho=m/V and p=(rho/mu)RT, equation4-3 label, retained and algebraically correct.
Pressure-density inference is approximate, temperature/species dependent, and refers to vapor rather than liquid or whole-system mean density.

Closed near-rigid heating, net evaporation and renewed equilibrium; increasing vapor density and temperature both contribute to pressure. Complete evaporation before criticality is conditional on filling/path, not universal; later proportionality to Kelvin is ideal-model only.
Liquid/vapor density branches and merging at criticality are stated along the lesson coexistence path, not arbitrary pressure/state heating.
Bubble growth/rise and surrounding hydrostatic pressure; local equilibrium, vapor-dominated bubbles, neglect of surface tension and nucleation/overheating qualifications stated.
Pressure-equality boiling criterion is a macroscopic approximation, not a guarantee of spontaneous nucleation in every clean liquid.

Higher absolute pressure raises boiling temperature within liquid-vapor scope. At200C water saturation pressure1.554928MPa is below16atm=1.6212MPa, so the nonboiling example is consistent. Historical medical vessel use is explicitly source-attributed, not a child procedure or sterilization guarantee.
Reduced-pressure room-temperature boiling and historical place attribution are sound; cooking universalization appropriately removed. Stated40kPa/70C pair is inconsistent: F1.

Pure-liquid comparison at common external pressure and no-mercury-experiment limit are sound. Normal mercury boiling point and100C mercury vapor pressure are incorrect: F2/F3. Water100C/one-atmosphere equality is acceptable textbook rounding, not a new erratum.

native_contract.boundary_assessment: All six adjacent native anchors exact: saturation law -> ideal approximation -> heating path -> critical densities -> boiling -> low-pressure examples -> cross-liquid comparison.

findings.modern_location: native paragraph23, historical mountain numerical example
findings.finding: Water boiling at approximately70C does not match the simultaneously stated40,000Pa (300mmHg). NIST water correlation gives75.8769C at40,000Pa; IAPWS95 data gives31,200.93Pa at70C. Attribution as original approximate data leaves a materially wrong pressure-temperature pairing in the modern lesson.

minimal_proposal.reason: At the source-stated absolute pressure near40kPa, pure-water equilibrium boiling temperature is about76C, not70C.
minimal_proposal.keep: Historical Pamir/Lenin Peak identity,7134m source altitude,40kPa/300mmHg and all unrelated text/formulas; clarify that corrected temperature is evaluated at the stated pressure, not a new mountain measurement.

findings.modern_location: native paragraph27, mercury boiling at one atmosphere
findings.finding: 375C is not the normal boiling point of mercury. NIST lists629.81K=356.66C;375C is about18.34C high. A source-only/unvalidated disclaimer is not sufficient for contemporary instructional data.

minimal_proposal.reason: Normal mercury boiling temperature629.81K rounds to357C, not375C.
minimal_proposal.wording: State approximately357C at one atmosphere, explicitly distinguishing corrected modern data from the original source value; retain the no-heating/no-experiment limit.

findings.modern_location: native paragraph27, mercury saturation pressure at100C
findings.finding: 117Pa=0.88mmHg is internally a consistent unit conversion, but is the wrong mercury saturation pressure at100C. NIST's Hicks-based Antoine fit gives37.7544Pa=0.283181mmHg within its valid temperature range; the source pressure is about3.10 times too large.

minimal_proposal.reason: Correct both members of the100C mercury vapor-pressure comparison using the evaluated correlation; keep temperature, water data and original units.
minimal_proposal.wording: Present the mercury pressure as approximately37.8Pa, approximately0.283mmHg; retain source attribution while identifying these as corrected values.
